text:
Zoe: Heads-up  Galaxy Insights (GI-900) wants a custom milestone billing schedule and an onboarding credit. They signed an SOW with milestone invoicing (50% upfront, 50% on deployment), but our billing system invoiced full amount upfront (INV-GI-9900 = $120,000). Customer asking: retro credit $60k and future invoices split per SOW, plus Net45 for milestone payments.

Liam: Looks like the billing integration ignored the SOW flag. CRM shows SOW type=milestone, but billing rule defaulted to standard recurring invoice. Support SR-8822 has the SOW PDF.

Carlos: This is material (> $10k) and touches revenue recognition. Need Deal Desk + Finance Lead + Legal sign-off. Also need to decide accounting treatment: is the $60k a credit or an invoice reissue? Reissuing impacts AR and audit trail.

Jill: Accounting prefers invoice reissue when possible to avoid contra-revenue noise. But reissuing for a closed billing period requires AR & Revenue Ops coordination. If reissue not possible, classify as contra-revenue GL 6601 (Invoice Reissue/Adjustments).

Zoe: Sales Ops says customer expects milestone schedule applied going forward and wants the retro adjustment as a credit memo if reissue delays. They're willing to accept a credit memo and policy note.

Carlos: Open Deal Desk DD-2027-310 with requested actions: 1) retro credit $60,000 (or invoice reissue if AR can), 2) apply milestone billing rule BR-GI-2027-01 for account GI-900 (50/50), 3) grant Net45 payment terms for milestone invoices only. Attach SOW and SR-8822. Tagging @Jill and @LegalBot.

LegalBot: Reviewing SOW. Legal note: SOW contains milestone billing terms and no conflicting payment terms. Legal approves honoring SOW billing mechanics. No contract amendment required; document decision in Deal Desk.

Jill: From accounting: prefer invoice reissue. I'll check if INV-GI-9900 can be voided and replaced with two invoices (INV-GI-9900-A $60k, INV-GI-9900-B $60k with Net45). If AR lock window prevents reissue, we will issue credit memo CM-GI-2027-04-01 and create two new invoices. Book adjustment under GL 6601.

Liam: Quick audit SQL for trail:
```
SELECT invoice_id, account_id, total_amount, created_at, billing_rule
FROM invoices
WHERE account_id = 'GI-900';
```
Result: INV-GI-9900, GI-900, 120000, 2027-03-29, default_recurring

Carlos: Finance provisionally approves the customer-facing outcome: honor SOW, apply milestone billing, and provide either invoice reissue or credit + new invoices. Final approval contingent on AR reissue feasibility. Add Finance note in DD-2027-310: approver=Carlos, GL=6601, memo='milestone billing adjustment per SOW; prefer reissue; credit if reissue blocked'.

Zoe: Customer message draft: "We will adjust your billing to match the SOW: we are splitting the billed amount into two milestone invoices and updating payment terms to Net45 for milestone invoices. If system constraints prevent immediate reissue, we will issue a credit memo and re-invoice per milestones. This does not change contract value." Shall I send? :email:

Jill: Hold until AR confirms reissue path. I'll run the reissue test in sandbox and report back by EOD.

BillingBot: requested action queued: create billing rule BR-GI-2027-01 (milestone 50/50) for account GI-900. Pending: AR reissue flag. Reference: #BR-GI-2027-01.

Jill: AR confirms reissue permitted for invoices within 60 days. INV-GI-9900 is within window. Proceeding to void and recreate invoices.

BillingBot: processed invoice reissue: voided INV-GI-9900; created INV-GI-9900-A (amount: $60,000, due upon receipt) and INV-GI-9900-B (amount: $60,000, due Net45). Posted at 2027-04-02T11:18:07Z. Reference: #INV-GI-9900-A, #INV-GI-9900-B.

Jill: Reissue complete. Accounting booked AR movement; no contra-revenue needed. Updated DD-2027-310 with outcome and GL closed as 1100 (AR movement).

Carlos: Closing DD-2027-310 as approved. Please send customer note and capture SOW billing lesson in the billing-run SOP to prevent regressions.

Zoe: Sent customer note and they confirmed receipt/acceptance. Marking SR-8822 resolved. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
